stem: Which clinical finding is most indicative of life-threatening asthma rather than severe asthma?

options.text: Soft or absent breath sounds on auscultation.
Inability to complete sentences in one breath.

explanation: Silent chest indicates such poor air movement that the situation has become life-threatening.
rationale: Think about what happens to audible air movement when a patient's respiratory effort becomes critically low.

optionExplanations.A: Oxygen levels in this range are characteristic of severe asthma, whereas life-threatening asthma involves levels below $90\%$.
optionExplanations.B: These signs indicate an increased work of breathing typical of the severe category.
optionExplanations.C: Silent chest indicates such poor air movement that the situation has become life-threatening.
optionExplanations.D: This level of respiratory distress is common in severe asthma but is superseded by findings like exhaustion or cyanosis in life-threatening cases.
